newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - August 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - August 2.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
GOVERNMENT ORDERS PROBE INTO ARMY AID FOR LALOO ARREST

The government took exception to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) seeking the army's assistance to arrest former Bihar state chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav and ordered an inquiry into the conduct of the concerned officials. Home Minister Indrajit Gupta told the upper house of parliament on Friday that the CBI officials' request to the local army authorities at Danapur had violated the established procedure and was wholly beyond their authority. But members belonging to the Samata Party, the Janata Dal and Samajwadi Party protested against the minister's statement. Samata Party leader Nitish Kumar accused the government of putting pressure on honest CBI officers who are investigating the fodder scandal.
The Economic Times
EUROPEAN UNION BANS INDIAN SEAFOOD IMPORTS

Despite India's last ditch efforts to postpone a ban, the European Union decided to ban imports of seafood from India from August 15, reports from Brussels say. This will hit exports worth eight billion rupees. But neither the Marine Products Export Development Authority nor the Seafood Exporters Association has any authentic information about the ban. Reports from Brussels say the European Union imposed a ban on seafood imports from Bangladesh on Wednesday and from India and Madagascar on Thursday. The decision is expected to be reviewed by the end of November.
TORRENT POWER SEEKS APPROVAL FOR OVERSEAS ISSUE

Torrent Power has sought government approval to issue preference shares of four billion rupees to foreign investors. United States-based MCN Corp will pick up a substantial part of the Torrent issue. It acquired a 40 percent stake in Torrent Power earlier this year. IG One of Mauritius, a subsidiary of MCN Corp, might also participate in the placement. Sources said the money would be invested in doubling the 655 megawatt capacity of the Paguthan power project in Gujarat state.
U.S. INSTITUTIONAL INVESTOR BUYS ASIAN PAINTS SHARES

A United States-based institutional investor bought 3.5 million shares of Asian Paints on the National Stock, about eight percent of Asian Paints' equity capital. The transaction, worth about 1.27 billion rupees, was negotiated and concluded on Thursday by DSP Merrill Lynch and was reported to the National bourse on Friday.
Financial Express
FOREIGN EQUITY ALLOWED IN FOREIGN EXCHANGE BROKING

The government will allow foreign exchange broking companies to share equity with overseas companies. The decision is expected to bring major foreign exchange broking companies into the country and boost cheap hedging products. The guidelines applicable for considering proposals of foreign equity participation in non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) will be equally applicable to foreign equity participation in foreign exchange broking. At present NBFCs are allowed foreign equity participation in 14 financial services including merchant banking, underwriting, portfolio management service, financial consultancy, stockbroking, asset management, venture capital firms and credit rating agencies.
INTERNET OPERATERS WILL NOT BE TAXED FOR TWO YEARS

The Telecom Commission has decided to allow private Internet service providers to do business without licence fees for the first two years of their operations. According to a new Internet policy adopted by the commission, licence fees will be waived for the first two years to promote the growth of Internet services. The new policy stipulates that international connectivity to Internet should be provided only through the local Internet gateways of the Department of Telecommunications or of India's international telecommunications service provider, Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL).
MOODY GIVES BAA3 RATING TO TATA POWER DEBT SECURITY

Moody's Investors Service gave Baa3 rating to the proposed issue of senior unsecured debt securities by Tata Power Co. The rating reflects Moody's expectation that the company management will continue to adhere to prudent financial practices. It also takes into account risks associated with customer concentration, deterioration in the company's balance sheet resulting from debt financing of capital expenditure, and the need to renew the Tata Electric Co's operating licence in 2014, three years before the final maturity of the securities.
Business Standard
EXPORTS UP BY 2.53 PCT IN JUNE

Exports during June increased by 2.53 percent year on year to $2.66 billion. This is considered a turnaround though the growth rate is lower than that of May's. A government note said the positive growth in exports in June indicated export optimism was likely to be sustained. An ambitious export target of $40 billion is set for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March).
CREDIT OFFTAKE SET TO PICK UP IN OCTOBER

State Bank of India chairman M.S. Verma on Friday said credit offtake would go up from October, buoyed by demand from the power industry. But there will be no significant change in credit offtake until October, he said. Verma said the automobile industry and the white goods sector appeared to be passing through a difficult phase. He said the decline in credit offtake during this fiscal year should be viewed against the backdrop of the wider menu available for firms to raise resources.
The Observer
GOVERNMENT UNDER PRESSURE TO RAISE BROAD MONEY GROWTH RATE

The Industry Ministry is putting pressure on the Finance Ministry to increase the rate of growth of broad money supply (M3) from 15.5 percent at present to overcome a slowdown in industrial production. The Industry Ministry and business representatives had analysed the declining trend in industrial growth two months ago. The industry representatives said they were forced to slash production due to lack of demand that arose from the curtailment of public expenditure and a tight monetary policy.
Business Line
RESERVE BANK BUYING DRIVES UP DOLLAR VERSUS RUPEE

The dollar/rupee market on Friday sprang to life after weeks of lacklustre and tight range-bound trading because of dollar-supportive intervention by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). With outright forward purchases estimated at around $50 million to $60 million, the RBI took the dollar all the way up to 35.75 rupees after opening at 35.70 rupees. Dealers said hectic inter-bank covering following the RBI action moved the dollar higher to 35.82 rupees.
